cues: Chloride is the conjugate base of hydrochloric acid, yet salt water is neutral.
Because hydrochloric acid is so strong, chloride is an extremely weak base, too weak to take protons back from water.
Conjugate describes a relationship, not a strength.
And one limitation remains: Bronsted needs a proton, so it cannot explain boron trifluoride reacting with ammonia.
